title: D-007: Decompose by Function, Not by Chunk Size
body:
# D-007: Decompose by Function, Not by Chunk Size

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Active

## Decision

Work decomposition assigns bounded functional roles to agents, not arbitrary word-count chunks to parallel workers.

## Why

Chunk-based decomposition produces voice inconsistency, requires complex merge logic, and produces outputs that are harder to quality-gate. Function-based decomposition (brief-writer, outline-architect, section-drafter, merge-normalizer) produces agents with clear scope, inspectable outputs, and composable pipelines.

The functional decomposition reflects the actual structure of document production as a discipline:
- Discovery and briefing are a distinct function from structural planning
- Structural planning (outline) is a distinct function from content generation (drafting)
- Content generation is a distinct function from normalization (merge)
- Normalization is a distinct function from quality evaluation (QA)
- Quality evaluation is a distinct function from artifact generation (export)

Each of these functions has different inputs, different outputs, different quality criteria, and different failure modes. An agent built for one function cannot be quality-gated the same way as an agent built for another. Chunk-based decomposition collapses these distinct functions into a single "write more words" operation and loses the auditability that phase-based function decomposition provides.

## Key Rule

Parallel section drafting is allowed — multiple section-drafter instances can run simultaneously on different sections of the same document — but voice normalization via merge-normalizer is always required after it. The merge-normalizer normalizes to the project voice pack, not to generic neutral. This means parallel drafting is a performance optimization that does not sacrifice quality, as long as the normalization step is not skipped.

## Alternatives Considered

**Chunk-based decomposition** (split the document into word-count buckets and assign each to a worker). Rejected: produces voice inconsistency proportional to the number of workers. Each worker develops its own local coherence, but the assembled document has no global coherence. Merge logic that tries to reconcile independently developed chunks is complex and still produces lower-quality output than function-based decomposition with a dedicated merge step.

## Consequences

A document production run involves more steps than a single-pass tool, but each step is auditable, resumable, and testable independently. Each agent's output can be validated against its schema, evaluated by the QA agents specific to its function, and cached for resumption if a later step fails. The function-based architecture also means that improving a single function (e.g., improving the outline-architect) improves all documents produced by the system without requiring changes to the other agents.
